words.gloss: even to those who harmed us

literal: Without doing harm, even to those who harmed us, if one does evil things after, inescapable distress it will bring.
translation: Even if others have caused us harm without any provocation, doing evil to them in return will bring us inescapable ruin.
modern: நமக்கு ஒரு தீங்கும் செய்யாமல் நமக்குத் தீங்கு செய்தவர்க்கும் நாம் திரும்பத் தீங்கு செய்தால், அது நமக்குத் தப்பிக்க முடியாத பெரும் துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute principle of non-injury. It warns that even if someone harms us without any provocation, returning that harm will only result in inescapable misery for ourselves. The word 'செற்றார்' refers to those who harbor anger or cause harm, while 'உய்யா' means that which cannot be escaped or cured. Thus, the poet shows that retaliation is self-destructive, bringing unavoidable ruin to the one who seeks revenge.
